audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart said Yasuo on all 7 rows while the content layer win[] and the packet levelChart say Xerath on all 7 — and every full-layer why already described Xerath winning the stage. The page rendered two opposite answers at every level.
audit.why: Packet chart, content layer, the 53.29% win rate and the whys all agree the stage-by-stage edge is Xerath's; only the side tokens were wrong.
audit.corrected: All 7 phases[N].side moved to Xerath with ratings 6/10 (5/10 late, where his flank threat peaks) and each why rewritten to be Yasuo-specific. win[N] already reads Xerath on every row, so no content edits (no-op pairs are rejected).

audit.why: All 4 spikes present and accurate: 3-5 wall-baiting, 6 Last Breath spacing, first-item punish window, late flank game.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers; missing interaction: his passive shield (Way of the Wanderer) absorbs the opening of your burst.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25s rank 1 / 17s maxed with a 4s block; his R is 70s rank 1. The passive shield triggers on champion damage, so one W tick pops it before the real trade.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns rewritten with real numbers; shield-pop line added to phases[1].why.

audit.why: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad under unrelated titles.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to match their titles with kit-grounded content.

edits.before: Q from fog-of-war range on his every last-hit — level 1 Xerath is the longest gun in the lane. Mana is the only governor.
edits.after: You outrange the melee wanderer completely — open with W chip Wind Wall can never block, Q behind it. Mana is the only governor.

edits.before: W joins the pattern: Q-W on the slowed target is the chip combo that defines the next twenty minutes.
edits.after: Q-W on the slowed target is the chip pattern — his passive shield pops to one W tick, then the trade is real.

edits.before: E completes the kill kit: the stun into full rotation is real damage even now. Hold it for HIS aggression, not yours.
edits.after: E completes the kit: hold the stun for his Sweeping Blade hops, not for poke — stunning the last dash ends his engage.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — the artillery goes infinite. Poke the wave contact, the trade attempt, and the recall walk.
edits.after: Lost Chapter — the artillery goes infinite. Bait Wind Wall with W, then tax its roughly 25s down-window with Q.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane online — chipped targets anywhere in the lane's zip code are now finishable. Shove and snipe.
edits.after: Rite online — but never barrage into a raised wall: zone his approach and snipe once Wind Wall is spent. Shove, then snipe.

edits.before: Luden's spike: Q-W chunks third-bars. He farms at half HP forever or he doesn't farm.
edits.after: Luden's spike: one clean Q past the wall chunks a third-bar. He farms at half HP or not at all.

edits.before: Late Xerath wins fights from the next postal code: stun the entry, barrage the objective, and never be seen.
edits.after: Late you win from the next postal code — stun his flank dash; one Wind Wall cannot cover a whole teamfight.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Shocking Orb has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Yasuo W Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1, 17s maxed, blocking for 4s — hold Q, E and R until it is spent; your W barrage falls through it. - His R Last Breath is 70s at rank 1. - Your E Shocking Orb has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. The R has one too: the moment it goes right.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: His E cannot re-hit the same minion for a few seconds, so the chain has a rhythm — stun the final hop, when no dash is left to dodge with.

edits.before: Spending E on chip and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive on schedule — the stun is your only 'no' and everyone knows it.
edits.after: A fat wave is a bridge: every minion is a Sweeping Blade hop and the third Q knockup arrives with Last Breath — keep the wave thin instead.

edits.before: Bait the wall with a throwaway Q
edits.after: Bait the wall with W, then land the Q

notes: Chart repair is the headline: full layer had Yasuo on all 7 rows against content win[] = Xerath x7, packet = Xerath x7, and whys describing Xerath winning. All sides moved to Xerath with matching why rewrites; content untouched because it was already correct. UNRESOLVED TENSION left alone: diff is HARD 8/10 and tone red while the chart, win rate (53.29%) and content layer all favour Xerath — diff/tone are mirror-coupled enums and I could not verify the yasuo-side entry, so I did not flip them; flagged for the user. dosFull[0].t said to bait the wall with Q, but Q is exactly what the wall blocks — retitled to bait with W (ground barrage, unblockable), matching dosFull[0].d and the content layer's advice.
